title: Dimension of an irreducible locally algebraic scheme over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be an irreducible scheme [def-weil-irreducible-components] whose structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then $\dim U=\dim X$ for every nonempty open subset $U\subseteq X$, and $\dim_x(X)=\dim X$ for every $x\in X$, where $\dim$ is the topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and $\dim_x$ is the dimension at a point [def-kun-dimension].

proof.text: (Reduction to $X$ integral.) Let $i:X_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$ be the reduction of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism] (with $X'=X$), $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and $i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] which is a homeomorphism of underlying spaces (indeed the identity on underlying sets). Hence $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] (being homeomorphic to $X$), so nonempty, reduced and irreducible, i.e. integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. A closed immersion is an immersion, hence locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] (2), so the composite $X_{\mathrm{red}}\xrightarrow{i}X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e). Every assertion of the lemma concerns only the topological space of $X$ (the Krull dimensions of open subsets with the subspace topology [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-kun-subspace-topology], and $\dim_x$ [def-kun-dimension], defined from them), and $i$ is a homeomorphism carrying nonempty opens to nonempty opens and preserving these dimensions [lem-weil-pbc-homeomorphism-krull-dimension]. Hence it suffices to prove the lemma for $X_{\mathrm{red}}$; from now on $X$ is integral and locally of finite type over $k$. (This is the source's parenthetical 'strictly speaking you have to replace $X$ by its reduction'.)

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), proof of part (3), last sentence: 'strictly speaking you have to replace X by its reduction before applying the lemma'

proof.text: For each nonempty open U of X, take its inverse image V in X_red. The reduction homeomorphism restricts to a homeomorphism V -> U, so V is nonempty and dim V = dim U. Apply [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension] to the integral scheme X_red and the locally finite type composite X_red -> X -> Spec k. It gives dim V = dim X_red, and the global homeomorphism gives dim X_red = dim X. Thus dim U = dim X.

For x in X, every open neighbourhood U contains x, so is nonempty. The preceding assertion says its dimension is dim X. By [def-kun-dimension], the infimum of those dimensions is dim X; implemented by the proved source helper topologicalKrullDimAt_eq_of_forall.

split_report.summary: Read Varieties 0A21 (varieties.tex line 3783) and the proof of part (3): reduce to X reduced, show any two nonempty affine opens have the same dimension (Jacobson 0478 gives a closed point in their intersection, Algebra 00OS gives dim U = dim O_{X,x} = dim U'), and conclude because any finite chain meets an affine open. Statement kept (it is part (3) verbatim with X irreducible). Steps: (1) replace X by X_red, integral and locally of finite type over k, same topological space; (2) the equal-dimension claim for affine opens, a new node attached to the sorry-free slopmaster2 declaration AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.topologicalKrullDim_eq_of_isIntegral (WeilConjectures/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/FiniteType.lean:123-134, checked with the sorry map); (3)-(4) dim U = d for every nonempty open U, via the affine basis, monotonicity on opens and Topology 0B7I (the source's 'any finite chain meets an affine open'); (5)-(6) the two assertions, the second from the definition of dim_x. Lean: slopmaster2 also has the integral form of the first assertion, AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_opens_eq (same file, lines 136-159, sorry-free); it does not state the item exactly (IsIntegral instead of irreducible) and is not attached to the item. Mathlib (pinned) has neither statement.
